atoms.title: The Piano
atoms.b: The piano is a keyboard instrument with 88 keys: 52 that are white and 36 that are black. The piano is played with both hands while sitting.
atoms.sound: The piano is a keyboard instrument with 88 keys: 52 that are white and 36 that are black. The piano is played with both hands while sitting.

atoms.b: When you press a key on a piano, you move a small hammer inside of the instrument. This hammer strikes a string inside of the piano, vibrating the string and creating a tone. This photo shows the small hammers above the piano strings inside of the piano.
atoms.sound: When you press a key on a piano, you move a small hammer inside of the instrument. This hammer strikes a string inside of the piano, vibrating the string and creating a tone. This photo shows the small hammers above the piano strings inside of the piano.

atoms.title: The Harpsichord
atoms.b: The harpsichord looks very similar to a piano. However, unlike the piano, the strings are not struck with a hammer, but are instead plucked with so-called plectra inside the instrument.
atoms.sound: The harpsichord looks very similar to a piano. However, unlike the piano, the strings are not struck with a hammer, but are instead plucked with so-called plectra inside the instrument.

atoms.b: When you press a harpsichord key, the plectra pluck the strings inside of the harpsichord and a tone is created.
atoms.sound: When you press a harpsichord key, the plectra pluck the strings inside of the harpsichord and a tone is created.

atoms.b: The harpsichord has a smaller pitch range than the piano and the tones of a harpsichord sound much brighter.
atoms.sound: The harpsichord has a smaller pitch range than the piano and the tones of a harpsichord sound much brighter.
